name: Tanzania
snapshot: After a 2025 election with the main opposition barred and hundreds reported killed in protests, Samia Suluhu Hassan's government faces its worst crisis of legitimacy.
culture: Swahili, the lingua franca of East Africa, is Tanzania's national language and a key part of the country's identity; founding president Julius Nyerere promoted it to unite more than 120 ethnic groups. Zanzibar's Stone Town, a centre of the old Indian Ocean trade, blends African, Arab and Indian culture. Bongo Flava is the country's hip-hop and pop.
society: Tanzania has long been among Africa's most peaceful countries. Tourism to Kilimanjaro, the Serengeti and Zanzibar, plus gold and farming, drive growth. Maasai communities have been evicted from Ngorongoro to make way for conservation and hunting, drawing international criticism.

story: For six decades Tanzania was East Africa's model of stability: the country of Julius Nyerere, never a coup, never a civil war, ruled throughout by the same party, CCM. When Samia Suluhu Hassan became its first woman president in 2021, after the death of the authoritarian John Magufuli, she promised reconciliation and loosened his crackdown. By the October 2025 election, she had reversed course.

The main opposition party, Chadema, was barred from the vote, and its leader Tundu Lissu, who survived 16 bullets in a 2017 assassination attempt, was arrested in April 2025 and charged with treason for campaigning under the slogan "No reforms, no elections." Samia won 98 percent. The largest protests in Tanzania's history followed, met with an internet blackout and mass killings; the opposition says about 700 or more died, rights groups say thousands (Gazette). In 2026 the reckoning has been one-sided. A government commission acknowledged 518 deaths but blamed "trained agitators" and "outside forces" and praised police restraint, findings even ruling-party members privately call ridiculous (The World This Wiki/Economist digest). Hundreds were charged with treason. Lawyers and rights groups have asked the International Criminal Court to investigate. On 21 August a court ruled Lissu has a case to answer; he faces a possible death sentence, represents himself, and has asked to call Samia as a defence witness (AFP via Africanews). The government's priority is growth and a long-delayed $40 billion gas project.
briefing.power: A presidential republic dominated by CCM since independence. The president is directly elected for up to two five-year terms and appoints a prime minister; Zanzibar has its own semi-autonomous government.
briefing.holders: President Samia Suluhu Hassan (CCM), since 2021; Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba.
